verdict.for_whom: Buy this if you want a fast-paced, aggressive shooter with an outstanding soundtrack and fluid movement, and do not mind a short campaign and a quiet multiplayer scene.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Players refunding early highlight the fast, aggressive combat mechanics where executing finishers drops essential resources. They enjoy the intense heavy metal soundtrack, though they point out that the campaign is quite short and report technical stability issues.

claims.claim: Reviewers report technical stability issues and random crashing on modern systems.

citations.review_text: Game is unstable on modern systems. fps drops from 200 to 17 fps at random times.

When I played under Windows 11 25H2, the game repeatedly crashed, even after following several steps on various forums. After 'upgrading' to Windows 10 to run the game, I found out you cannot earn XP on their supposedly dead multiplayer component, without a mod. I add that mod, and game crashes after selecting a class.

The campaign component is probably worth it, but at full price should be a crime. Just another broken game I cannot believe is still being sold. Avoid this garbage if you can. If you like the Campaign, consider getting it on GOG, which will also be DRM free.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the campaign length as short, noting it can be beaten in roughly six hours.

citations.review_text:
A great action game that rarely lets you catch your breath. The gunplay is fluid and fast-paced, and extremely satisfying!
The game pushes you to play aggressively. Finishers drop health and ammo, which sets up a really satisfying gameplay loop. 
Mick Gordon's heavy metal OST is an absolute banger, ofc. It runs super well on PC.

I wish it lasted a bit longer, as it will only take you maybe 6 hours to beat.

Overall, a well-crafted experience and an awesome FPS game. I did prefer DOOM Eternal, but I would still highly recommend DOOM (2016)!

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: In the initial hours, players experience smooth performance and high optimization even on older hardware, although they encounter stability issues like crashing when tabbing out and occasionally get lost in levels.

claims.claim: Reviewers report getting stuck on level geometry such as railings and wandering around levels when trying to find the correct path forward.

citations.review_text:
I played this game after playing Eternal and I see where a lot of the core gameplay came from. My biggest gripe with the game is the railing as I feel like I'm constantly getting stuck on them. I think that it feels quite slow compared to Eternal and Doom 1 & 2. I also think the chainsaw and BFG having 3 shots is a bit OP. I think if you get this game on sale or play it before playing Eternal you'll have a great time but honestly I love Eternal so this game isn't nearly as good in comparison in my opinion. 

Overall if you haven't played Eternal or Dark Ages, play Doom 2016, if you have, then just pass over the game.
The immersive game missions are great, but sometimes it becomes a frustrating when you can't understand which path to follow to proceed in the game

I owned Doom on console years ago, but when I saw it on sale on Steam, there was no way I wasn’t buying it again. It had been probably five or six years since I last played, and within the first few minutes it all came rushing back.

The combat still feels insanely good, the soundtrack still hits like a truck, and hearing that music start building before a big fight never gets old. You know there’s a solid chance you’re about to get your ♥♥♥♥ rocked by whatever’s behind the next door... and somehow that just makes it even more fun.

My only real gripe is that some levels had me wandering around longer than I’d like, trying to figure out where the hell the game wanted me to go. One minute I’m tearing through demons like a machine, the next I’m checking the same hallway for the third time.

Still, coming back to it after all these years reminded me exactly why I loved it in the first place. Easy 4/5 Doom Guys from me.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that finding secrets and collectibles in the levels is difficult.

citations.review_text: decent story. A little repetitive with same bad guys over and over.  great FPS overall.  Hard to find any of the secrets.  Some rune trials were really impossible

Doom 2016 is definitelly a big step up compared to any previous Doom games. It's a Doom for totally new modern audience. There is plenty to praise, but the game has it's faults, no doubt about that. The weapons don't feel particularry powerful even with max upgrades, which takes the edge of slaying demons, the gameplay is sometimes dull (when you run around not killing demons and no music is playing, the game feels very ordinary). Also it gets quite repetitive by the end since as I mentioned above the weapons feel weak and you are fighting the same enemies in the same pattern (first wave is weaker enemies, second wave are top enemies). But if you like collecting all the secrets and other collectibles, you will have plenty of fun with that, since you have no chance of finding them all on one playthrough. For a second playthrough, when I was collecting everything I could and upgrading my suit and weapons, the game was definitelly more fun. Especially when you get to the point you can have infinite ammo under certain conditions. The there's not enough demons to slay.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the campaign lacks regenerating health and cover mechanics, instead requiring constant movement and aggression.

citations.review_text:
Maybe one of the single greatest FPS games released. DOOM follows in the footsteps of it's forefathers, defying FPS standards while also defining the bar for what makes a good shooter. DOOM will make you question everything about playing an FPS, there is no cover, no ADS, no regenerating health and no mercy. 
A nice change of pace, and a breath of fresh air every time I open it.

I finally got around to playing DOOM, and it absolutely lives up to the hype. The combat is fast, aggressive, and constantly pushes you to stay on the move instead of hiding behind cover. Every weapon feels great to use, and the game does an awesome job of making you feel stronger as you unlock new abilities.
The story definitely takes a backseat, but that's clearly not the focus. It's all about the gameplay, and it delivers from start to finish. The soundtrack is incredible, the level design keeps things fresh, and every fight feels like pure chaos in the best way. It's one of those games that's just ridiculously fun to play and never gets old.

[h1] Just kill them all [/h1] 
This game taught other first-person shooters how it should be done. No hiding behind cover, no recovering health. Shoot and destroy, or you will be destroyed.

[h3]  Pros: [/h3] 
Action Speed: The game is very dynamic. The "Glory Kills" system works perfectly – forcing the player into close combat for health and ammo.

[b]Weapons: [/b] They are very powerful. From a typical shotgun to the iconic BFG, each shot makes the player feel powerful. Alongside weapon mods, there are special mini-challenges, such as: Kill two enemies consecutively with a shotgun for 15 times.

[b]Music:[/b] Mick Gordon's soundtrack fits the game perfectly. Industrial metal makes me feel like I am about to blow my head up in the process of getting into a fight. Exactly what I expect and want from this game.

[b]Optimization:[/b] The game looks fantastic and runs well even on weaker machines.

[h3] Cons:[/h3] 
[b]Environments:[/b] Mars environment was cool and unique, but once you get to Hell, all locations start looking the same – mainly consisting of red and brown colors.

[b]Multiplayer: [/b] This part isn't perfect. It looks forced and, of course, cannot compete with single-player game quality-wise.

[b]Boss Fights:[/b] There aren't many of them. As you face them after unlocking all the weaponry, the boss fights tend to be too easy.

[h3] Is it worth recommending? [/h3] 
I would say yes. Despite being based only on killing, the game is extremely fun. If you wish to switch off your brain and have some plain fun, this is what you should choose.

[b] My Rating: 8/10 ⭐ [b]

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features optimization that allows it to run smoothly at high frame rates and on older hardware.

citations.review_text: I am impressed with how well optimized this game is!! It ran at 200fps for me. And what a magnificent game. The level degisn, the gunplay, the enemies, everything was perfect down to the last minute detail!

If you want a slick, gritty and heavy metal shooter following the gameplay of the good old days totally maxed out but featuring great graphics and a great OST by Mick Gordon, this is it. DOOM 2016 pretty much started the still ongoing comeback of "boomer" shooters while innovating quite a bit and it still is among the very best in the genre (next to Dusk, Selaco, Amid Evil and others). Only thing that could have been better are the rather pathetic grenades but you can pretty much ignore them if you don't care about them.

Anyone enjoying shooters that focus on gameplay should try DOOM 2016. Performs really well on Linux and older hardware, too!
